advisories.title: Update Node.js for the Brotli security fix
advisories.message: Affected Node.js releases contain a Brotli decompression vulnerability. Use Node.js 22.23.4, 24.22.1 or 26.12.1, or a later patched release. Refreshing images only helps if your configured image or Dockerfile supplies the patched runtime. Review pinned versions, rebuild, and check the deployed runtime again.

advisories.title: Update Bun for the Brotli security fix
advisories.message: Bun versions before 1.4.4 include the affected Brotli decoder. Upgrade to Bun 1.4.4 or later. Refreshing images only helps if your configured image or Dockerfile supplies the patched runtime. Review pinned versions, rebuild, and check the deployed runtime again.

advisories.title: Update PHP for the October 21 RCE fixes
advisories.message: PHP 8.2.35, 8.3.36, 8.4.27 and 8.5.12 fix CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619. Update your runtime image and restart every worker through deployment. A pinned vulnerable version must be changed first. Vendor backports need vendor verification. Also review the separate session upload progress guidance published on October 23; a version update alone does not resolve that follow-up.

advisories.title: PHP session upload progress: conditional review
advisories.message:
PHP 8.2.35, 8.3.36, 8.4.27 and 8.5.12 fix the October 21 vulnerabilities. This separate follow-up is a conditional configuration review; it does not mean that the image update failed or that this app is confirmed vulnerable.

CVE-2026-115560 applies only when session upload progress is enabled and the app starts with session.serialize_handler set to php_binary or php_serialize, then switches it to php with ini_set() before session_start(). Applications that never change the handler this way do not need a setting change. Upload progress being enabled alone does not establish exposure.

If those conditions apply, set session.upload_progress.enabled=0 in PHP server startup configuration before request parsing and restart all affected workers. OpenShip's runtime-version observation cannot verify these configuration and application conditions; review the official guidance before changing a service.
